hooks.text: An Earth-sized world makes a year in six days.
Seven Earth-sized planets would all fit inside Mercury's orbit.
A distant exoplanet heats itself with currents 100,000 times stronger than Earth.

title: The Planet With a Six Day Year
description: Discover TRAPPIST-1e, an Earth-sized exoplanet with a scorching six-day year that actively strips away its own atmosphere.

beats.text: An Earth-sized world makes a year in six days.
beats.visual: Artist concept of exoplanet TRAPPIST-1e surface showing red dwarf in sky, 2017

beats.text: It orbits an ultracool red dwarf forty light-years away.
beats.visual: Artist concept of ultracool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1 and its orbiting planets, 2017

beats.text: All seven planets in the system would fit inside Mercury's orbit.
beats.visual: Diagram comparing TRAPPIST-1 planetary orbits to the inner solar system, 2017

beats.text: This tiny world is likely locked facing its star forever.
beats.visual: Size comparison diagram of seven TRAPPIST-1 planets and Earth, 2017

beats.text: Rapid motion drives electric currents heating its upper atmosphere.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope during deployment illustration, 2021

beats.text: It generates heating 100,000 times stronger than Earth experiences.
beats.visual: Spitzer Space Telescope observing in space illustration, 2003

beats.text: The planet actively strips away its own atmosphere over time.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope orbiting Earth photograph, 2009

beats.text: That is how a year in six days dooms an entire world.
beats.visual: TRAPPIST telescope dome at La Silla Observatory in Chile, 2010
